summary: Harusawa Hinata, a struggling 25-year-old web designer, still misses talented childhood friend Otonashi Sora, who disappeared eight years earlier after leaving a note about traveling to develop his art. After former art-club senior Shinohara announces that Sora has been found, Hinata attends Sora's wake and overhears former club leaders Hase and Tokiwa reveal that his skeleton was concealed inside their high school's art-room wall. Hinata realizes Sora was likely murdered when he disappeared and suspects someone from the art club. After examining Sora's last known painting, Shinohara is found gravely wounded and urges Hinata to protect it, mentioning a secret and Sora's murderer. While trying to safeguard the painting and seek help, Hinata is attacked by an unidentified assailant and loses consciousness. Hinata awakens eight years in the past, in the spring of the second year of high school, and resolves to save Sora, who is alive and working on that painting, with 180 days remaining before his disappearance.

After being attacked at his childhood friend Otonashi Sora’s funeral and traveling eight years back to high school, 25-year-old Harusawa Hinata has 173 days to prevent Sora’s November 10 disappearance, murder, and concealment inside the art-room wall. Hinata suspects art-club vice president Tokiwa, who fears Sora’s painting will prevent him from winning the National Teen Art Award and entering Kamakura Art School, successes he achieved after Sora vanished in the original timeline. Tokiwa confronts Sora with a cutter, Sora provocatively discusses dying to understand Christopher Wood’s final painting, Zebra and Parachute, and Hinata intervenes and is injured. Sora explains that Tokiwa intended to damage his painting and that his disturbing remarks were a diversion, prompting Tokiwa to admit his jealousy and apologize. Tokiwa insists on reporting himself to their advisor, Mr. Hakuraku, and Hinata concludes that he is unlikely to be Sora’s murderer. The chapter ends with a sudden crash and an apparent tragedy involving Tokiwa that never happened in the original timeline, leaving Hinata wondering whether his intervention caused it.

Hinata and Sora visit Vice President Tokiwa, whose severe arm and eye injuries threaten his future as an artist, leaving Hinata guilty about changing the timeline. Sora restores Tokiwa’s hope by suggesting he enter Kamakura Art School’s cultural studies course and transfer to oil painting after recovering. Tokiwa privately reveals that someone pushed him and suspects President Hase because he saw a tattoo near the attacker’s armpit, matching her interest in hidden henna tattoos. Hinata wonders whether Hase is also responsible for Sora’s future murder and the attacks on himself and Shinohara, and plans to check her arm during a temple sketch outing where he remembers her falling into a pond. At the outing, Hase goes missing, and Hinata finds her in the pond and pulls her out. He suspects another attack, making him question whether Hase is really the culprit.

Hinata tells President Hase that he has recovered after nearly drowning, suffered no other injuries, and stayed in the school infirmary. Hase expresses relief, and a request to speak with Hinata is followed by an apology. Later, an unnamed speaker questions how Sora knows the future and is alarmed by his reference to his "last work." An unfinished suspicion about Sora and an emphatic denial leave the situation unresolved.

Four months after Sora disappears leaving only a note, his childhood friend Hinata remains distraught as their art club’s seniors graduate. Tokiwa, newly accepted into Kamakura Art School, says Sora would have won the Teen Art Award had he submitted his painting, then joins Hase and Shinohara in treating Hinata to a waffle after his remarks make him cry. Reflecting on his lack of future plans beyond staying with Sora, Hinata recalls Sora’s childhood wish to join his family and their hope of remaining together forever. Hinata then finds himself before Sora’s disappearance, discussing Sora’s competition painting and their future together, and promising to visit the waffle shop with him. The chapter ends with Hinata realizing he has somehow traveled back in time and beginning an unfinished declaration: “This time, I’ll—”.

Hinata discovers Sora’s secret cabin, which Sora describes as experimental installation art, but a blood-like smell leaves Hinata suspicious. With 145 days until Sora’s future disappearance, Hinata resolves to disrupt the planned murder, concealment of Sora’s body inside a wall, and forged goodbye letter. The art club resumes activities, while Hase and Tokiwa conceal their attacks to protect the club and discuss a tattoo seen on the attacker. Hinata creates an installation titled “Everything Will Be Exposed” to provoke the culprit, but Sora is the only person visibly disturbed and suddenly collapses. Watching over his unconscious friend, Hinata suspects that Sora already knows he will be murdered. The chapter ends with Shinohara telling Hinata to accompany her to the art room if he wants to prevent Sora’s death, shocking him with her apparent knowledge of the future.

Shinohara warns Hinata that Sora may be planning suicide, citing his remarks about painting with his own and another person's blood and his interest in artists who killed themselves. Hinata knows from the original timeline that Sora will be murdered and struggles to reconcile this warning with Sora's disappearance and the attacks on the art club president and vice president. After art club supervisor Hakuraku Issei drives away a stranger seeking interviews with the injured students, Hinata carries an exhausted Sora home, hoping to support him without pressing him for answers. At Sora's house, Hinata discovers a calendar defaced around November 10, Sora's expected disappearance date, and a flight reservation to Hokkaido, where Sora's parents live, for the day after his predicted murder. Outside, the stranger identifies himself as a Gangan Gossip reporter investigating an alleged school cover-up involving a student's fall from a window and another student's near drowning. The chapter ends with the reporter claiming that Hakuraku killed someone in Hokkaido years ago and offering to reveal the teacher's past to Hinata.
A content restriction prevented me from providing the requested summary. I can offer a general overview focused on the characters and investigation.

Ch.9: Kizuki tells Hinata he had heard of a gifted, increasingly unstable student at Souzou College of Arts in Sapporo and of over-zealous mentors there, but never pursued the story; he regrets it. They fly to New Chitose and follow Hakuraku, who goes not to the university but to a residential area: the house Sora's parents moved to. Hinata confronts him with a bluff ('I know everything'); Hakuraku weeps that Sora would never betray him, calls the two of them one in body and soul, then brightens and leads Hinata inside. The house is abandoned and reeks; Hakuraku shows him two coffins and calls them Sora's masterpiece. Kizuki phones: someone in Hinata's school uniform stabbed him and is heading to Hinata. Hinata is stabbed from behind -- not by Hakuraku -- remembers the same stench near Sora's cabin, and wakes at Sora's funeral eight years later, having failed to change the future.

At Sora’s funeral, Harusawa Hinata learns that his altered past left him unconscious for eight years, while Hakuraku disappeared and was blamed for the Hokkaido attack. Reunited with his surviving art club friends, Hinata tells reporter Kizuki about his time travel and persuades him to help prevent Shinohara’s murder. Although Kizuki briefly lets Shinohara wander off to test Hinata’s prediction, they interrupt a suspicious man’s approach and save Shinohara, convincing Kizuki that Hinata is telling the truth. Hinata then discovers that Sora’s painting has vanished and suspects the original attacks were intended to let the culprit steal it. Back at his parents’ home, he resolves to find a way back to the past, but half a month later Kizuki reveals that the body hidden in the art room wall was Hakuraku’s, not Sora’s.

Kizuki tells Hinata that hair discovered in the art-room wall identifies the hidden remains as Mr. Hakuraku's, previously mistaken for Otonashi Sora's because of a uniform fragment. They suspect the student who stabbed them eight years earlier, and Hinata resolves to return to the past to prevent all three tragedies. Shinohara visits Hinata and reveals that the apple in Sora's final painting appears to have been painted with blood, increasing suspicions about Sora. Hinata theorizes that Sora is alive and stole the painting from his own funeral to finish it before it could be cremated, while the tattooed man who attacked the vice president remains a mystery. On his way home, Shinohara realizes that another clue to Sora's secret is hidden in the painting and tries to contact Hinata. Before he can explain, Shinohara is struck by a train after apparently being pushed onto the tracks, and an unidentified person tells him not to put unnecessary ideas into Hinata's head.

After Shinohara's funeral, Harusawa Hinata learns from reporter Kizuki that police evidence shows Otonashi Sora, previously believed dead, pushed Shinohara onto the railway tracks. Hinata resolves to meet the present-day Sora and understand his motive before returning to the past to stop him and save Shinohara. He reveals his time-leaping experiences to former art club president Hase and vice president Tokiwa, who agree to help; Hase also confesses her longtime love for Shinohara and asks Hinata to save him. They spread a false rumor that Hinata is leaving to study art abroad, hoping to lure out Sora, whom Hinata suspects needs his blood to finish the apple in his missing painting. Two weeks later, as Hinata privately considers whether another attack could trigger a time leap, Sora appears and greets him.

At the Enoshima Iwaya Caves, Hinata confronts Sora after their reunion following eight years apart, and Sora admits responsibility for Hakuraku’s death, the art club’s accidents, the stabbing of Hinata and Kizuki, and Shinohara’s death. Sora recounts how his abusive parents blamed him for ruining their careers, repeatedly wished him dead, and forced him to conceal his suffering. His childhood friendship with Hinata and their shared love of drawing became his sole source of happiness, leading him to love Hinata and wish to stay with him forever. When Hinata suggested attending art university together, Sora’s parents instead announced a move to Hokkaido and refused to let him attend university, making Sora see them as enemies threatening to take Hinata away. The flashback ends with Sora fleeing home and encountering Mr. Hakuraku at the art club late at night, an encounter he says would lead to him being swallowed up by Hakuraku.

Mr. Hakuraku praises Sora’s artwork and gains his trust by offering support over his parents’ emotional abuse, but secretly hopes to use Sora’s despair to create his ideal “art of death.” At his home, Hakuraku deepens Sora’s fear of losing Hinata and, when Sora talks about ending his life, proposes an undisclosed plan to strike back at his parents and stay with Hinata forever. Following Hakuraku’s instructions, Sora pretends to become obedient and persuades his parents to let him spend the summer in Kamakura before joining them in Hokkaido. After enjoying summer with Hinata, Sora receives reassurance that Hinata wants to remain with him throughout their lives, strengthening his resolve to carry out the plan. Sora then travels to Hokkaido, and the chapter ends with him telling Hakuraku that he has “finished,” without revealing what he has done.

After murdering his parents, Sora feels relieved and believes he has become a monster, while his teacher Hakuraku encourages him to create a final painting using his and Hinata’s blood and die together with Hinata. Hakuraku helps conceal the murders, but his attacks on the art club’s president and vice president arouse Hinata’s suspicions, eventually bringing Hinata to Sora’s house in Hokkaido, where Sora panics and stabs him. Hakuraku reassures Sora that Hinata did not see his attacker and sends Sora back to Kamakura; Hakuraku becomes a fugitive blamed for the stabbing, Hinata remains in a coma, and the school suspends art club activities. Troubled by his friends’ kindness and Hinata’s plea to confide in him, Sora recognizes his fear of being condemned and decides he no longer wants to die with Hinata. He summons Hakuraku, announces his change of heart, and reveals that he murdered Hakuraku that night.

Sora reveals that he once abandoned his plan to die with Hinata out of fear of being hated, but Hakuraku manipulated him into continuing by making his own death part of Sora’s murderous artwork; Sora then concealed Hakuraku’s body and waited eight years for another opportunity. Hinata refuses to condemn Sora for what his parents and Hakuraku drove him to do, but insists that killing Shinohara was wrong and urges him to live and atone. Unable to accept this limit to Hinata’s acceptance, Sora attempts to drown them together while pleading not to be left alone. Hinata initially believes Sora’s attempts to kill him trigger his time leaps, then realizes the true trigger may be Sora’s cry for help and promises to save him. He awakens in his own room believing he has returned to the past, but senses something unusual and reacts in shock as he prepares to leave for school.

Hinata time-leaps sixteen years into the past, becoming his nine-year-old self eight years before Sora's disappearance, and resolves to save Sora from his abusive parents and prevent the future murders. Despite the restrictions of childhood, he gets Sora to admit his suffering and ask for help, hoping to involve social services. However, Sora's mother overhears their conversation and has Sora admitted to a psychiatric hospital, dismissing his allegations as imagination and announcing plans to change his school and end his art lessons. Hinata's plan to record evidence of the abuse is thwarted, leaving him devastated that his intervention has isolated Sora further. The chapter ends with Hinata deciding to seek help from an unnamed person, despite believing that contacting him is dangerous.

One week after Sora is hospitalized, Hinata travels alone to Hokkaido to stop Hakuraku's influence and prevent Sora from becoming a murderer in the future. He hopes that exposing Sora's parents' abuse and stopping Hakuraku's first crime will change the future, possibly ending his time-leaping ability. At the university where Hakuraku lectures, Hinata identifies Hiroki as the troubled student destined to die by suicide and overhears Hakuraku tell him that he looks forward to their dying together. Hinata follows Hiroki to the atelier, discovers him writing a message expressing fear of Hakuraku, and intervenes in his suicide attempt. When Hinata explains that he wants to save both Hiroki and a friend suffering similarly, Hiroki agrees to tell his story and reveals that he became close to Hakuraku after the professor's own suicide attempt, and that Hakuraku has wanted to die ever since.

Hiroki explains that Professor Hakuraku was once a kind painting teacher, but changed after his parents and grandfather died in a house fire, which he survived. After Hiroki confronted his abusive teaching and inadvertently triggered his trauma, Hakuraku revealed a past suicide attempt, leaving Hiroki feeling guilty and unable to refuse his demands to paint increasingly beautiful depictions of death. Hiroki eventually learned that Hakuraku wanted a final masterpiece to glorify his own suicide and hoped Hiroki would die with him; fearing that another student would become his replacement, Hiroki remained trapped and became suicidal himself. In the present, Hakuraku interrupts the confession, and Hiroki's young listener confronts him, demanding that he stop involving Hiroki and Sora in his death wish. Hakuraku angrily accuses the child of obstructing his plan, and the chapter ends with a sudden slash as Hiroki cries out for him to stop, leaving the outcome unclear.

Hakuraku stabs Hinata, but Hiroki rejects Hakuraku's obsession with death and intervenes to help the wounded child. Hinata desperately calls out to Sora, who senses his danger and wishes for them to be saved together, triggering another time leap. Now even younger, Hinata arrives at the fire that killed Hakuraku's family and helps them escape through an upstairs window, hoping to prevent Hakuraku's trauma and change Sora's future. Hakuraku returns and enters the burning house to rescue his family, and Hinata saves him from falling debris before struggling to breathe and hearing Sora call him again. Hinata awakens wearing a school uniform in a scene resembling his very first time leap, with Sora asking whether he likes his painting, and reacts in surprise to Sora and the artwork.

Hinata realizes he has changed the future when Sora’s once death-driven painting becomes bright and hopeful, and their club supervisor is no longer Hakuraku. Sora now lives in a supportive group home away from his parents and hopes his art will encourage other children like him. Hinata also learns that Hakuraku Issei is now a successful artist whose desire to live stems from a mysterious boy saving him and his family from a fire, confirming that Hinata’s efforts succeeded. Their peaceful school days resume, the date of Sora’s disappearance passes safely, and Tokki wins the Teen Art Award’s gold prize while Sora receives the jury’s special award. As graduation approaches, Hinata recognizes the old painting’s connection to Caravaggio and its overlooked plea for help, bids farewell to the tragic futures he prevented, and moves forward together with Sora.

In the afterword, the author explains that the volume was created to save Sora and Hinata and convey hope for their happy future. In the closing scene, Hinata vents about a client who keeps demanding revisions, while Sora praises his willingness to listen to requests and redraw his work. They discover that the former art club members' sketch gathering is happening that day, and Shinohara apologizes for giving Sora the wrong date. Hinata decides his work can wait as long as he delivers it by the beginning of the following week, and they hurry to join the gathering.
